To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
254-nm ultraviolet light induces p21 protein and concomitantly arrests G1 phase in human skin fibroblast cell cultures that are either normal or p53-deficient.
UV light induces p53-independent G1 arrest in human skin fibroblast cell culture.
UV irradiation induces p21(waif1cip1) and G1 arrest in human skin fibroblast cell lines that are deficient in functional p53 protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms by which DNA-damaging radiation and chemicals cause growth arrest in human cells.
the mechanisms of DNA damage-induced G1 arrest in human skin fibroblast cells.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate cell cycle progression in normal human cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
UV light-induced p21(waf)1cip1 expression is p53-dependent in normal fibroblast, but p53-independent in Li-Fraumenii fibroblasts.
p21(waf/cip1)-mediated G1 arrest is a p53-independent process, but p21(waf) induction is p53 dependent.
p21(waf) is induced in a p53-independent manner following DNA damage by UV light.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
p21(waf) is a critical mediator of G1 arrest in response to UV irradiation, but that p53 is dispensable for this response.
p21(waf-1cip1) induction and growth arrest in UV- or gamma-irradiated cells is dependent on the p53 status of the cells.
p21(waf 1cip1) induction by DNA-damaging radiation can occur by two separate pathways: a p53-dependent one and a p53-independent one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
p53-independent pathways exist for the induction of G1 arrest following DNA damage.
p21(waf)1cip1 is induced in a p53-independent manner by UV light in cultured human skin fibroblast cells.
the p53-dependent and p53-independent pathways for p21 induction and G1 arrest are distinct, but can both be activated by UV radiation.
